review_comments.body:
- if there is an exception - it make sense to throw it when detected. 
- strings like `exception` should be a constants 
- ServerException should not be constructed with assumed code if it is unknown - it should be constant and somethin like `-1` otherwise it will be hard to handle different exceptions.
this method would be somewhere in ClientUtils or similar. There are different code formats and we usually check for some string - not just dot.

please replicate this logic from clickhouse-js https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/1085/changes#diff-a25af8931a1e9a25e3aa2ba71bfcc1f11cb4ab875e902b7100d17009250bdc52R76

This is most recent one and should work with different version

we may not guarantee the order and we should make another check. 
besides - here we could also check type.
and even more optimize because schema not changing - so we can bake another condition.

please convert to integration tests. 
Unit tests do not verify client behavior with different database versions.

this should be under feature flag because currently it is on hot path. 
exception will be different in most cases when deserialization happens - so this feature doesn't not add much value. 
having an option to read server code is good - but only as option.

### IT hardcodes plaintext HTTP on cloud **Medium Severity** `httpBody` always opens `http://` against `getServer(HTTP)`, while `setUp` builds the `Client` with `isCloud()` so cloud runs use TLS. On cloud that node is an HTTPS endpoint, so `testOptInThrowsTheServerCodeAfterDataRows` and `testDetectionOffReturnsTheExceptionRowAsData` never reach a real in-band body.
Additional Locations (1) - [`client-v2/src/test/java/com/clickhouse/client/api/data_formats/JSONEachRowServerExceptionIT.java#L48-L57`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-java/blob/5f4a7d41d1aaaa5a9abdd561e8ac8a7e5b711ea5/client-v2/src/test/java/com/clickhouse/client/api/data_formats/JSONEachRowServerExceptionIT.java#L48-L57)

Thanks for the review. I pushed an update.

Detection is off by default. You have to use `new JSONEachRowFormatReader(parser, true)` to turn it on. The schema is decided from the first row, so the normal path doesn't do extra checks.

When the option is on, a row is treated as an error only if it has exactly one entry, the key is `exception`, and the value is a String that looks like a ClickHouse error (starts with `Code: ` or `Error: ` and has a numeric code).

`JsonParser.nextRow()` already returns a parsed map, so we can't look at the raw line. The row in the issue is valid JSON, so the parser doesn't fail. The check only looks at that map and doesn't change the parser.

If the result schema is a single String column named `exception`, we leave it as data. A body that is only the exception object has the same shape, so it also stays data; `Client.query()` already throws when the response is just the exception.

The one-argument constructor is unchanged and doesn't inspect rows. jdbc-v2 `StatementImpl` uses that constructor, so it keeps the old behavior.

Reproduction on ClickHouse 25.8:

```sql
SELECT toInt32(number) AS id FROM numbers(100)
WHERE throwIf(number = 50, 'in-band-boom') = 0
SETTINGS http_write_exception_in_output_format = 1, max_block_size = 1
FORMAT JSONEachRow
```

Tests:
- `JSONEachRowFormatReaderTest` and `ClientUtilsTest` cover the opt-in flag, the schema exception, `Code:` / `Error:` parsing, and a `Code:` value that is not an exception text.
- `JSONEachRowServerExceptionIT` runs on ClickHouse 25.8 with both Gson and Jackson. With the option on, it throws after the data rows. With the option off, the exception row comes back as data. A real `exception` column stays data.

This change was prepared with the assistance of an AI tool (Claude).

Thanks, both points addressed in 3c663ad: the integration test now reads the body through `Client.query()` instead of a raw `HttpURLConnection` (no hand-built Basic auth or plain-HTTP request), and `setUp()` throws `SkipException` when running on Cloud. Following a run against a real server (26.10), the test client also sets `compressServerResponse(false)`: with a compressed response the server buffers the body and answers with HTTP 500 + `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code`, so no in-band exception row is streamed. The latest commit (e7dc0e6) adds that and drops a stale javadoc; the IT passes 6/6.
